topics.title: Anatomy & Physiology
topics.subtitle: Heart circulation, lungs, renal nephron, brain lobes, body planes & cell organelles

questions.prompt: Which heart valve prevents backflow from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular systole?
questions.rationale: The mitral (bicuspid) valve lies between the left atrium and left ventricle and closes tightly during systole.

questions.prompt: Which chamber of the heart receives oxygenated blood directly from the four pulmonary veins?
questions.rationale: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs via four pulmonary veins into the left atrium.

questions.prompt: A sagittal plane divides the human body into which two parts?
questions.rationale: A sagittal plane runs vertically front-to-back to divide the body into left and right portions.

questions.prompt: What is the functional filtration unit of the kidney?
questions.rationale: Each kidney contains roughly 1 million nephrons responsible for filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is primarily responsible for ATP synthesis via aerobic cellular respiration?
questions.rationale: Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.prompt: Primary gas exchange of O2 and CO2 occurs across which respiratory structure?
questions.rationale: Thin Type I pneumocytes and capillary endothelium allow rapid O2/CO2 diffusion across alveoli.

questions.prompt: Which lobe of the cerebral cortex processes primary visual input from the optic tracts?
questions.rationale: The occipital lobe at the posterior cerebrum houses the primary visual cortex.

questions.prompt: Which blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?
questions.rationale: The pulmonary arteries are the only arteries in postnatal circulation carrying deoxygenated blood.

questions.prompt: Which endocrine gland releases antidiuretic hormone (ADH) and oxytocin into systemic circulation?
questions.rationale: Hypothalamic neurons synthesize ADH and oxytocin, which are stored and released by the posterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: Where are digestive enzymes such as amylase, lipase, and trypsinogen produced?
questions.rationale: Pancreatic acinar cells secrete amylase, lipase, and proteases into the duodenum.

questions.prompt: Which bone forms the posterior-inferior portion of the cranial base surrounding the foramen magnum?
questions.rationale: The occipital bone encloses the foramen magnum where the spinal cord exits the skull.

questions.prompt: Normal resting adult cardiac output averages approximately:
questions.rationale: Cardiac Output = Heart Rate × Stroke Volume, averaging 4–8 L/min at rest.

questions.prompt: In the anatomical position, the palms of the hands are facing:
questions.rationale: Standard anatomical position: standing upright, feet parallel, arms at sides, palms facing forward.

questions.prompt: Which type of muscle tissue is striated and involuntary?
questions.rationale: Cardiac muscle exhibits striations and intercalated discs under involuntary autonomic control.

questions.prompt: Which cranial nerve mediates the sense of hearing and equilibrium?
questions.rationale: CN VIII transmits cochlear (auditory) and vestibular (balance) signals.

questions.prompt: Intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption, is secreted by which cells of the stomach?
questions.rationale: Gastric parietal cells secrete both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.

questions.prompt: What is the normal lifespan of a human erythrocyte (red blood cell)?
questions.rationale: Mature erythrocytes circulate for ~120 days before splenic macrophages clear them.

questions.prompt: The pacemaker that normally initiates every cardiac electrical impulse is the:
questions.rationale: The sinoatrial (SA) node in the right atrium fires at 60–100 bpm as the natural pacemaker.

questions.prompt: Bile is synthesized by hepatocytes in the liver and concentrated in the:
questions.rationale: The liver produces bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it until fat enters the duodenum.

questions.prompt: Select ALL structures that belong to the upper respiratory tract:
questions.rationale: The nasal cavity, pharynx, and larynx form the upper respiratory tract; alveoli belong to the lower respiratory tract.

questions.prompt: Select ALL hormones secreted by the anterior pituitary gland:
questions.rationale: TSH, ACTH, and Prolactin are anterior pituitary hormones; Oxytocin is released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.prompt: Select ALL functions of the human integumentary system (skin):
questions.rationale: Skin regulates temperature, synthesizes vitamin D, and detects touch/pain; bile is made by the liver.

questions.prompt: Select ALL cranial nerves involved in extraocular eye movement:
questions.rationale: CN III, IV, and VI control eye muscles; CN IX innervates pharynx/taste.

questions.prompt: A transverse (axial) plane divides the body into superior (upper) and inferior (lower) sections.
questions.rationale: True: transverse planes run horizontally to separate superior from inferior structures.

questions.prompt: The left lung normally has three lobes while the right lung has two lobes.
questions.rationale: False: the right lung has 3 lobes (superior, middle, inferior) and the left lung has 2 lobes to accommodate the heart.

questions.prompt: Erythropoietin, which stimulates red blood cell production in bone marrow, is primarily secreted by the kidneys.
questions.rationale: True: peritubular kidney cells release erythropoietin in response to hypoxia.

questions.prompt: Smooth muscle is found exclusively in the heart wall.
questions.rationale: False: cardiac muscle forms the heart wall; smooth muscle lines hollow organs and blood vessels.

topics.title: Foundations of Nursing & Health Assessment
topics.subtitle: ADPIE nursing process, vital signs, IPPA physical exam, asepsis & wound care

questions.prompt: Which step of the ADPIE nursing process comes immediately after Assessment?
questions.rationale: The 5 steps follow Assessment → Diagnosis → Planning → Implementation → Evaluation.

questions.prompt: During an abdominal physical examination, what is the correct assessment sequence?
questions.rationale: Auscultate the abdomen BEFORE palpation/percussion so bowel sounds are not artificially altered or pain triggered.

questions.prompt: Which adult radial pulse rate should the nurse document as tachycardia?
questions.rationale: Normal adult resting pulse is 60–100 bpm; > 100 bpm is tachycardia.

questions.prompt: When cleaning a non-infected surgical incision, the nurse should wipe:
options: From the outer edges inward toward the incision
Directly back and forth along the same swab
From the cleanest area (incision) outward to surrounding skin
Circularly starting at the drain site toward the suture line
questions.rationale: Sterile wound cleansing always moves from cleanest (least contaminated) to dirtiest area.

questions.prompt: Which patient position best relieves dyspnoea and improves lung expansion?
questions.rationale: High-Fowler's lowers the diaphragm via gravity and maximizes thoracic expansion.

questions.prompt: For an adult ear otoscope exam, how should the nurse pull the pinna?
questions.rationale: Adult ear canal: pull pinna UP and BACK. In children under 3 years, pull DOWN and BACK.

questions.prompt: Which finding on pulse oximetry requires immediate clinical intervention?
questions.rationale: Normal SpO2 is 95–100%; < 90% signifies critical hypoxemia.

questions.prompt: According to WHO 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene, when must alcohol hand rub or soap washing occur?
options: Before patient contact, before aseptic task, after body fluid exposure, after patient contact & surroundings
questions.rationale: All 5 WHO moments prevent healthcare-associated infections.

questions.prompt: Which nursing intervention prevents pressure ulcers in an immobile stroke patient?
options: Reposition the patient at least every 2 hours
Elevate head of bed to 90 degrees continuously
Use donut-shaped air cushions under the sacrum
questions.rationale: Repositioning q2h relieves capillary occlusion; massaging reddened tissue worsens shear injury.

questions.prompt: Which blood pressure reading meets criteria for adult hypertension (two separate readings)?
questions.rationale: BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg on repeated readings defines hypertension.

questions.prompt: A NANDA nursing diagnosis written in P-E-S format includes:
options: Problem, Etiology (Related to), Signs/Symptoms (As evidenced by)
questions.rationale: PES links the nursing Problem to its Etiology and observable Evidence.

questions.prompt: How long should a nurse scrub hands with soap and running water during routine hygienic handwashing?
questions.rationale: WHO guidelines specify 40–60 seconds for soap-and-water handwashing (20–30s for alcohol rub).

questions.prompt: Which thermometer route provides the closest core body temperature but is contraindicated in neutropenia or cardiac arrhythmia?
questions.rationale: Rectal temperature reflects core heat accurately but risks mucosal trauma or vagal bradycardia.

questions.prompt: When removing sterile PPE, which item is normally contaminated most and removed FIRST?
questions.rationale: Gloves carry highest surface contamination and are removed first to avoid contaminating skin/face.

questions.prompt: When collecting a clean-catch midstream urine culture specimen, the patient should:
options: Collect the very first drops of urine
Void a small amount into toilet first, then catch midstream in sterile cup
Add tap water to dilute concentrated urine
questions.rationale: Voiding initially flushes distal urethral flora so midstream reflects bladder urine.

questions.prompt: What is the normal adult respiratory rate?
questions.rationale: Eupnea (normal adult breathing) is 12–20 breaths/min.

questions.prompt: In documentation, if a medication dose was omitted because the patient vomited, the nurse should:
options: Leave the chart blank until tomorrow
Record the omission, reason, vitals, and provider notification accurately
Use correction fluid to erase the scheduled row
questions.rationale: Legal nursing records require factual, timely, non-erased documentation of omissions and rationale.

questions.prompt: Contact precautions (gown + gloves) are specifically mandatory for which condition?
options: MRSA wound infection or Clostridioides difficile diarrhea
questions.rationale: Contact precautions prevent direct/indirect transfer of MRSA, C. diff, or scabies.

questions.prompt: Which assessment finding demonstrates objective rather than subjective data?
options: Measured blood pressure 88/54 mmHg and diaphoresis
questions.rationale: Measured vitals and observable physical signs are objective data.

questions.prompt: Select ALL components of a SMART nursing planning goal:
questions.rationale: Effective care plans set Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic, and Time-bound goals.

questions.prompt: Select ALL correct sterile field rules in nursing procedures:
options: Never turn your back on an open sterile field
Objects below waist level are considered contaminated
The outer 2.5 cm (1 inch) border is non-sterile
You may reach directly across a sterile tray if wearing clean gloves
questions.rationale: Never reach across a sterile field; keep everything dry, above waist, and within direct sight.

questions.prompt: Select ALL Priority ABCDE assessment actions:
options: C — Check pulse, capillary refill & hemorrhage
E — Skip exposure to save time
questions.rationale: ABCDE requires Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability (neuro/glucose), and full Exposure while preventing hypothermia.

questions.prompt: Select ALL symptoms commonly associated with hypovolemic shock:
questions.rationale: Hypovolemia triggers tachycardia, low BP, cool skin, and oliguria (< 30 mL/hr).

questions.prompt: Airborne precautions require a negative-pressure isolation room and an N95 respirator when caring for infectious pulmonary tuberculosis.
questions.rationale: True: M. tuberculosis spreads via droplet nuclei < 5 microns requiring airborne precautions.

questions.prompt: Using a blood pressure cuff that is too narrow for a patient's arm produces a falsely LOW blood pressure reading.
questions.rationale: False: a too-narrow cuff yields a falsely HIGH BP reading.

questions.prompt: A nurse should evaluate patient progress continuously rather than waiting solely until discharge.
questions.rationale: True: evaluation in ADPIE is ongoing to adjust care promptly.

questions.prompt: Normal adult capillary refill time is longer than 5 seconds.
questions.rationale: False: normal capillary refill is < 2 seconds.

topics.title: Midwifery & Maternal Health
topics.subtitle: Antenatal care, partograph, 4 stages of labour, AMTSL, PPH & pre-eclampsia

questions.prompt: Under WHO/Uganda Active Management of Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL), what uterotonic is given immediately after delivery of the baby (after ruling out twins)?
questions.rationale: WHO recommends Oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 minute of birth as the uterotonic of choice.

questions.prompt: On a WHO Partograph, crossing the Action Line indicates:
options: Urgent medical intervention/review for prolonged or obstructed labour
questions.rationale: Crossing the Action Line (4 hours right of Alert Line) demands immediate obstetric intervention.

questions.prompt: What is the normal baseline fetal heart rate (FHR) range?
questions.rationale: Normal term fetal heart rate is 110–160 bpm.

questions.prompt: Which drug is first-line to prevent and stop eclamptic seizures in severe pre-eclampsia?
questions.rationale: Magnesium Sulfate is the WHO gold standard anticonvulsant in eclampsia/severe pre-eclampsia.

questions.prompt: Before giving a maintenance dose of Magnesium Sulfate, what must the midwife verify?
options: Urine output ≥ 30 mL/hr, Respiratory rate ≥ 16/min, and present patellar reflex
questions.rationale: Loss of patellar reflex, RR < 16, or urine output < 30 mL/hr signals MgSO4 toxicity (antidote: Calcium Gluconate).

questions.prompt: Primary Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) is defined after vaginal delivery as blood loss equal to or greater than:
questions.rationale: PPH is ≥ 500 mL after vaginal birth (or ≥ 1,000 mL after cesarean section) within 24 hours.

questions.prompt: What is the MOST common cause of primary postpartum hemorrhage (the leading 'T' of the 4 Ts)?
questions.rationale: Uterine atony accounts for ~70–80% of primary PPH cases.

questions.prompt: At what cervical dilation does the Active Phase of First Stage of Labour begin on the modern partograph?
questions.rationale: Latent phase is 0–3 cm; Active phase runs from 4 cm to full 10 cm dilation.

questions.prompt: Which fetal lie and presentation is safest and most common for spontaneous vaginal birth?
options: Longitudinal lie with cephalic vertex presentation
questions.rationale: Longitudinal lie with flexed vertex presentation presents the smallest suboccipitobregmatic diameter (9.5 cm).

questions.prompt: Which vaccine is routinely given to pregnant mothers in Uganda to prevent neonatal tetanus?
questions.rationale: Td vaccination during pregnancy protects both mother and newborn via transplacental IgG antibodies.

questions.prompt: In PMTCT (Option B+) in Uganda, HIV-positive pregnant mothers should:
options: Start or continue lifelong triple ART regardless of CD4 count
questions.rationale: Option B+ provides lifelong ART to suppress maternal viral load and prevent vertical transmission.

questions.prompt: Using Naegele's Rule, if LMP began on 10 March 2026, what is the Estimated Date of Delivery (EDD)?
questions.rationale: Naegele's Rule: LMP + 7 days + 9 months = March 10 + 7 days = March 17 + 9 months = Dec 17.

questions.prompt: Which maneuver defines the Third Stage of Labour placental delivery?
options: Controlled Cord Traction (CCT) with uterine counter-traction
questions.rationale: Controlled Cord Traction while applying upward suprapubic counter-traction prevents uterine inversion.

questions.prompt: What does a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg plus 3+ proteinuria at 34 weeks gestation indicate?
questions.rationale: Severe hypertension + proteinuria after 20 weeks = Severe Pre-eclampsia.

questions.prompt: During an APGAR assessment at 1 minute, a newborn has pink body/blue extremities, HR 130, active crying, good flexion, and sneezes with suction. What is the APGAR score?
questions.rationale: Appearance (1 for acrocyanosis), Pulse (2), Grimace (2), Activity (2), Respiration (2) = 9/10.

questions.prompt: When performing fundal massage for uterine atony, the uterus should feel:
options: Soft and boggy above the umbilicus
Firm like a contracted grapefruit in the midline
Deviated sharply to the right groin
questions.rationale: A firm contracted uterus compresses spiral arteries to arrest bleeding.

questions.prompt: In shoulder dystocia emergency, what is the immediate first maternal positioning maneuver?
options: McRoberts maneuver (hyperflex maternal thighs onto abdomen) + suprapubic pressure
questions.rationale: McRoberts flattens the sacral promontory and rotates the symphysis pubis upward; NEVER apply fundal pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended minimum duration for Exclusive Breastfeeding under WHO & Uganda MoH guidelines?
questions.rationale: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months gives optimal nutrition, passive IgA immunity, and lactational amenorrhea support.

questions.prompt: Painless bright-red vaginal bleeding in the third trimester (at 32 weeks) is classically suspicious for:
questions.rationale: Placenta previa causes painless bright-red bleeding; NEVER perform a digital vaginal exam before ultrasound rules it out.

questions.prompt: Select ALL classic signs of Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) toxicity:
options: Absent or diminished patellar (deep tendon) reflexes
questions.rationale: MgSO4 toxicity presents with areflexia, respiratory depression, and oliguria.

questions.prompt: Select ALL warning/danger signs in pregnancy requiring immediate hospital evaluation:
options: Absence or marked decrease in fetal movements
Mild morning ankle edema after standing
questions.rationale: Bleeding, visual/headache signs (pre-eclampsia), and absent fetal movements are obstetric emergencies.

questions.prompt: Select ALL steps of the Newborn Essential Thermal & Airway Care immediately at birth:
options: Dry the baby thoroughly and remove wet cloth
Initiate skin-to-skin contact on mother's chest
Monitor breathing/tone and initiate breastfeeding within 1 hour
Bathe baby in cool water within 5 minutes of birth
questions.rationale: Delay bathing for at least 24 hours to prevent neonatal hypothermia.

questions.prompt: Select ALL components included in the 4 Ts of Postpartum Hemorrhage:
questions.rationale: The 4 Ts are Tone, Trauma, Tissue, and Thrombin.

questions.prompt: Digital vaginal examination should be performed immediately when placenta previa is suspected to assess cervical dilation.
questions.rationale: False: digital vaginal exam in placenta previa can cause catastrophic hemorrhage.

questions.prompt: Oxytocin should NOT be given if an undelivered second twin remains inside the uterus.
questions.rationale: True: wait until confirming there is no second twin before administering prophylactic oxytocin in AMTSL.

questions.prompt: The antidote for Magnesium Sulfate toxicity is Calcium Gluconate 10% (1g IV slowly).
questions.rationale: True: Calcium Gluconate reverses neuromuscular blockade caused by hypermagnesemia.

questions.prompt: Puerperal sepsis typically presents within the first 6 weeks after childbirth or miscarriage with fever, foul-smelling lochia, and subinvolution.
questions.rationale: True: puerperal infection requires prompt broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and uterine evaluation.

topics.title: Clinical Pharmacology & Drug Calculations
topics.subtitle: Pharmacokinetics ADME, dosage formulas, IV drip rates, antibiotics & antidotes

questions.prompt: A prescriber orders 500 mg Amoxicillin PO. Stock tablets are 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?
questions.rationale: (Desired 500 mg ÷ Stock 250 mg) × 1 tablet = 2 tablets.

questions.prompt: 1,000 mL Normal Saline is ordered over 8 hours using a macrodrip set of 15 drops/mL. What is the correct drip rate?
Which organ is the primary site of First-Pass Drug Metabolism for oral medications?
questions.rationale: Oral drugs enter the portal vein to the liver before reaching systemic circulation.

questions.prompt: Which antidote reverses acute opioid-induced respiratory depression?
questions.rationale: Naloxone is a competitive mu-opioid receptor antagonist.

questions.prompt: Which medication is first-line for Severe Uncomplicated & Complicated Malaria in Uganda (parenteral)?
questions.rationale: IV/IM Artesunate is Uganda Clinical Guidelines first-line treatment for severe malaria.

questions.prompt: For an adult experiencing acute anaphylactic shock, what is the immediate first-line drug and route?
options: Epinephrine (Adrenaline) 0.5 mg IM (1:1000) into anterolateral thigh
questions.rationale: IM Epinephrine 1:1000 into the mid-outer thigh is life-saving in anaphylaxis.

questions.prompt: Which organ failure prolongs drug half-life most dangerously for aminoglycosides like Gentamicin?
questions.rationale: Gentamicin is almost exclusively renally excreted and is nephrotoxic/ototoxic.

questions.prompt: In the standard adult patient, a normal therapeutic INR range for Warfarin anticoagulation is typically:
questions.rationale: Most DVT/PE/AF indications target INR 2.0–3.0; excess INR is reversed with Vitamin K.

questions.prompt: Which oral anti-TB drug turns urine, tears, and sweat harmlessly orange-red?
questions.rationale: Counsel TB patients that Rifampicin turns body fluids orange-red and reduces oral contraceptive efficacy.

questions.prompt: Which adverse effect should nurses monitor for with Isoniazid (INH), prevented by Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6)?
questions.rationale: Give Pyridoxine (Vit B6) alongside Isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy.

questions.prompt: Before administering Digoxin to a cardiac patient, the nurse checks apical pulse for 1 full minute and holds the dose if pulse is:
questions.rationale: Hold Digoxin if adult apical HR < 60 bpm or signs of toxicity (yellow halos, nausea) appear.

questions.prompt: Which class of antihypertensives can cause dry persistent cough and angioedema by accumulating bradykinin?
questions.rationale: ACE inhibitors elevate bradykinin; switch to an ARB (e.g., Losartan) if dry cough develops.

questions.prompt: Which insulin has the fastest onset (10–15 minutes) and must be given right before eating?
questions.rationale: Rapid-acting analogs peak within 1–2h; never administer unless meal is present.

questions.prompt: What electrolyte abnormality is caused by Furosemide (Loop diuretic) and increases Digoxin toxicity risk?
questions.rationale: Furosemide wastes K+; hypokalemia sensitizes myocardium to Digoxin toxicity.

questions.prompt: Which medication is contraindicated in pregnancy because it causes fetal teratogenic neural/kidney defects or premature ductus closure?
questions.rationale: Warfarin and ACE inhibitors are teratogenic; switch anticoagulation to LMWH/Heparin and HTN to Methyldopa/Nifedipine.

questions.prompt: A nurse reconstitutes Ceftriaxone 1g with 10 mL sterile water. How many mL contain a prescribed 500 mg dose?
Why should patients taking Metronidazole strictly avoid alcohol?
questions.rationale: Metronidazole inhibits aldehyde dehydrogenase, triggering severe disulfiram reactions with alcohol.

questions.prompt: Which bronchodilator provides rapid rescue relief during an acute asthma attack?
questions.rationale: Salbutamol relaxes bronchial smooth muscle within minutes.

questions.prompt: Which oral antibiotic stains developing teeth and impairs bone growth in children under 8 years and pregnant women?
questions.rationale: Tetracyclines chelate calcium in developing teeth and fetal bone.

questions.prompt: Select ALL components of the 4 processes of Pharmacokinetics (ADME):
questions.rationale: Pharmacokinetics studies what the body does to a drug: ADME.

questions.prompt: Select ALL essential Rights of Safe Medication Administration:
questions.rationale: Always verify Patient, Drug, Dose, Route, Time, Documentation, Education, Assessment, Evaluation & Right to Refuse.

questions.prompt: Select ALL anti-tuberculosis drugs included in the RHZE first-line intensive phase:
questions.rationale: RHZE stands for Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide, and Ethambutol.

questions.prompt: Select ALL valid routes for parenteral injection:
questions.rationale: IM, SC, ID, and IV are parenteral (injected) routes; sublingual is enteral/mucosal.

questions.prompt: Intravenous (IV) drugs have 100% bioavailability and bypass the hepatic first-pass effect.
questions.rationale: True: IV administration places drug directly into systemic circulation.

questions.prompt: Alcohol should always be encouraged to wash down oral analgesics like Paracetamol.
questions.rationale: False: alcohol markedly increases Paracetamol hepatotoxicity.

questions.prompt: Vitamin K (Phytomenadione) is the specific reversal agent for Warfarin overdose.
questions.rationale: True: Vitamin K restores hepatic clotting factor synthesis (II, VII, IX, X).

questions.prompt: Patients on Ethambutol must be counseled to report blurred vision or red-green color changes immediately.
questions.rationale: True: Ethambutol can cause dose-dependent optic neuritis.

topics.title: Medical-Surgical Nursing
topics.subtitle: Diabetes/DKA, hypertension, stroke, heart failure, shock, fractures & GI emergencies

questions.prompt: Which classic triad characterizes Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
options: Hyperglycemia, ketosis/ketonuria, and metabolic acidosis (Kussmaul breathing)
questions.rationale: DKA presents with hyperglycemia, ketone production, and high anion-gap metabolic acidosis.

questions.prompt: What is the FIRST priority intervention for a patient arriving in Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
options: IV isotonic Normal Saline (0.9% NaCl) fluid resuscitation
questions.rationale: Restore intravascular volume with IV 0.9% NaCl first, followed by IV Regular Insulin + K+ monitoring.

questions.prompt: Using the Wallace Rule of Nines, what is the burn %TBSA of an adult with burns over the entire anterior trunk and entire right leg?
questions.rationale: Anterior trunk = 18% + Entire right leg = 18% = 36% TBSA.

questions.prompt: Using the Parkland Formula (4 mL × kg × %TBSA), how much fluid is needed in the FIRST 8 hours for a 70 kg adult with a 20% burn?
questions.rationale: Total 24h = 4 × 70 × 20 = 5,600 mL; 50% is given in the first 8 hours = 2,800 mL.

questions.prompt: Which clinical sign indicates impending Hypovolemic or Compensated Septic Shock?
options: Narrowing pulse pressure, tachycardia, cool extremities, capillary refill > 3s
questions.rationale: Sympathetic vasoconstriction causes tachycardia, cool clammy skin, and rising diastolic pressure initially.

questions.prompt: In a patient with an acute ischemic stroke, what must be obtained BEFORE considering thrombolytic therapy?
options: Non-contrast Head CT scan to rule out intracranial hemorrhage
questions.rationale: Hemorrhagic vs ischemic stroke look identical clinically; CT rules out bleed.

questions.prompt: Which assessment sign suggests right-sided Heart Failure rather than isolated left-sided Heart Failure?
options: Jugular venous distention (JVD), hepatomegaly, and bilateral ankle edema
questions.rationale: Right heart failure backs up into systemic veins (JVD, liver congestion, peripheral edema).

questions.prompt: A patient presents with sudden severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and serum amylase 4× normal. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Elevated amylase/lipase > 3× normal + epigastric pain radiating to back = Acute Pancreatitis.

questions.prompt: Pain out of proportion to injury, tense swollen limb, paresthesia, and pain on passive stretch after a tibial fracture signify:
questions.rationale: Compartment syndrome threatens limb ischemia; loosen tight casts immediately and notify surgeon for fasciotomy.

questions.prompt: Which cardiac biomarker is most specific and remains elevated longest (7–10 days) after acute Myocardial Infarction?
questions.rationale: Cardiac Troponin I/T rises within 3–6 hours and stays elevated 7–10 days.

questions.prompt: Murphy's sign (inspiratory arrest when palpating right upper quadrant under costal margin) points to:
questions.rationale: Painful arrest when the inflamed gallbladder touches palpating fingers indicates cholecystitis.

questions.prompt: Rebound tenderness at McBurney's point in the Right Lower Quadrant is classic for:
questions.rationale: McBurney's point sits 1/3 the distance from right ASIS to umbilicus.

questions.prompt: Which nursing care step is vital for a patient with a closed chest tube drainage system (water-seal)?
options: Clamp the tube continuously during transport
Keep the drainage chamber below chest level and monitor gentle tidaling
Raise the drainage bottle above the bed
Empty the water-seal fluid every hour
questions.rationale: Never clamp routinely; keep below chest level to prevent fluid reflux and tension pneumothorax.

questions.prompt: Which ECG finding demands immediate defibrillation (shockable cardiac arrest rhythm)?
questions.rationale: Shockable rhythms are V-fib and pulseless V-tach; Asystole/PEA require CPR + Epinephrine (not shock).

questions.prompt: What does Trousseau's sign (carpal spasm on BP cuff inflation) or Chvostek's sign indicate?
questions.rationale: Neuromuscular excitability after thyroidectomy signals hypocalcemia (low PTH).

questions.prompt: A patient with COPD should receive oxygen titrated carefully (target SpO2 88–92%) because excess oxygen can:
options: Blunt hypoxic respiratory drive and worsen CO2 retention
questions.rationale: Controlled low-flow O2 prevents hypercapnic narcosis in chronic CO2 retainers.

questions.prompt: In benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causing acute urinary retention, the priority nursing action is:
options: Insert a urinary catheter (Foley) under strict asepsis to decompress bladder
questions.rationale: Decompress bladder smoothly; monitor for post-obstructive diuresis.

questions.prompt: Which sign confirms suspected meningitis on bedside physical exam?
options: Nuchal rigidity (neck stiffness), Kernig's & Brudzinski's signs + fever
questions.rationale: Meningeal irritation triggers nuchal rigidity, positive Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs.

questions.prompt: When caring for an acute upper GI bleed (hematemesis / melena), the immediate nurse priority is:
options: Assess airway, establish 2 large-bore IV lines, crossmatch blood, and give isotonic fluids
questions.rationale: Stabilize Airway and Circulation (fluids/PRBCs) first; avoid NSAIDs.

questions.prompt: Select ALL components of Beck's Triad for Cardiac Tamponade:
questions.rationale: Beck's triad: Hypotension + JVD + Muffled heart sounds.

questions.prompt: Select ALL classic warning signs of Stroke (BE-FAST):
options: Speech slurring — Time to act fast
questions.rationale: BE-FAST speeds early stroke recognition for urgent CT/thrombolysis.

questions.prompt: Select ALL priority nursing measures for Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT) prevention post-operatively:
options: Vigorously massaging the painful swollen calf
questions.rationale: NEVER massage a suspected DVT leg as it can dislodge a fatal Pulmonary Embolism.

questions.prompt: Select ALL triggers or manifestations of Thyroid Storm:
questions.rationale: Thyroid storm is life-threatening hypermetabolism with fever, tachycardia, and delirium.

questions.prompt: A patient with left-sided heart failure typically develops pulmonary congestion, crackles, and orthopnea.
questions.rationale: True: left ventricular failure backs pressure up into the pulmonary veins and lungs.

questions.prompt: In acute appendicitis, applying a hot heating pad to the abdomen is recommended to speed recovery.
questions.rationale: False: heat increases vasodilation and risks rupture/peritonitis.

questions.prompt: Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD) is most commonly caused by Helicobacter pylori infection and chronic NSAID use.
questions.rationale: True: treat H. pylori with triple/quadruple therapy and stop offending NSAIDs.

questions.prompt: Post-operative bowel sounds typically return immediately within 5 minutes of general abdominal anesthesia.
questions.rationale: False: paralytic ileus commonly delays normal bowel sounds for 24–72 hours post-op.

topics.title: Paediatrics & Child Health
topics.subtitle: IMCI triage, UNEPI immunization, neonatal resuscitation, malnutrition & ORS

questions.prompt: According to Uganda IMCI guidelines, which finding is an immediate General Danger Sign requiring urgent Pink hospital referral?
options: Convulsions, lethargy/unconsciousness, vomiting everything, or unable to drink/breastfeed
questions.rationale: Any General Danger Sign classifies as Severe Disease (Pink) requiring pre-referral care and urgent transfer.

questions.prompt: Under the UNEPI (Uganda National Expanded Programme on Immunization) schedule, which vaccines are given at BIRTH?
options: BCG (right upper arm ID) and OPV 0
questions.rationale: At birth: BCG intradermally + OPV 0 oral.

questions.prompt: Which MUAC (Mid-Upper Arm Circumference) measurement in a 2-year-old child indicates Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)?
questions.rationale: MUAC < 11.5 cm (or bilateral pitting oedema) defines Severe Acute Malnutrition.

questions.prompt: What is the key nutritional hallmark distinguishing Kwashiorkor from Marasmus?
options: Marked bilateral pitting edema, hepatomegaly, flaky-paint dermatitis & 'moon face'
Extreme severe muscle/fat wasting ('skin and bones') with alert hungry appearance
questions.rationale: Kwashiorkor is protein-deficiency oedematous malnutrition; Marasmus is total calorie wasting.

questions.prompt: In Uganda Clinical Guidelines, what is the first-line management for a child with Moderate (Some) Dehydration from acute diarrhea?
options: Low-osmolarity ORS (75 mL/kg over 4 hours) + Zinc supplementation (10–20 mg/day for 10–14 days)
questions.rationale: Never give antimotility drugs in children; give ORS + Zinc 20 mg/day (10 mg if < 6 months).

questions.prompt: When resuscitating a newborn who is not breathing and has HR < 100 bpm after drying & stimulation, what is the FIRST priority within the Golden Minute?
options: Positive-Pressure Ventilation (Bag-and-Mask) at 40–60 breaths/min with room air
questions.rationale: Ventilating newborn lungs with bag-and-mask within 60 seconds is the #1 resuscitation action.

questions.prompt: At what age is the first Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine routinely administered in Uganda?
questions.rationale: MR is administered subcutaneously at 9 months (and booster at 18 months).

questions.prompt: Which sign distinguishes Pneumonia from a simple cough/cold in a 10-month-old infant under IMCI?
options: Fast breathing (>= 50 breaths/min for age 2–11 months) or lower chest wall indrawing
questions.rationale: Respiratory rate cutoffs: < 2m >= 60/min; 2–11m >= 50/min; 1–5y >= 40/min.

questions.prompt: Which clinical sign defines Severe Malaria in a child rather than uncomplicated malaria?
options: Prostration, convulsions, impaired consciousness, severe anemia (Hb < 5 g/dL), or hypoglycemia
questions.rationale: Cerebral malaria / severe anemia / respiratory distress require parenteral IV Artesunate immediately.

questions.prompt: What is the correct chest compression to ventilation ratio when performing CPR on a neonate with HR < 60 bpm despite 30s effective PPV?
questions.rationale: Neonatal resuscitation uses a 3:1 compression-to-ventilation ratio.

questions.prompt: When assessing a sick infant aged 2 months to 5 years for Dehydration, which signs confirm SEVERE dehydration?
options: Lethargic/unconscious, sunken eyes, unable to drink, skin pinch goes back VERY slowly (> 2 seconds)
questions.rationale: Two or more severe dehydration signs demand immediate Plan C IV Ringer's Lactate resuscitation.

questions.prompt: For a preterm low-birth-weight newborn in Uganda, Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) primarily prevents:
options: Hypothermia, hypoglycemia, and neonatal sepsis while promoting weight gain
questions.rationale: Skin-to-skin KMC stabilizes temperature, supports breastfeeding, and improves preterm survival.

questions.prompt: Which classic symptom characterizes Croup (Acute Laryngotracheobronchitis) in toddlers?
options: Inspiratory stridor and a harsh 'barking seal' cough worse at night
questions.rationale: Subglottic edema in parainfluenza virus produces barking cough and stridor (treat with Dexamethasone).

questions.prompt: What is the preferred first-line antibiotic for non-severe Pneumonia in Ugandan children aged 2–59 months?
options: Oral Amoxicillin dispersible tablets (DT) for 5 days
questions.rationale: Uganda MoH / WHO IMCI recommends high-dose oral Amoxicillin DT for outpatient pediatric pneumonia.

questions.prompt: Which finding on physical exam of a newborn should prompt suspicion of Congenital Heart Disease?
options: Central cyanosis (tongue/lips), tachypnea with sweating during feeds, and loud heart murmur
questions.rationale: Central cyanosis and feeding fatigue point to congenital cardiac shunts or failure.

questions.prompt: Phototherapy is used to treat Neonatal Jaundice primarily to prevent bilirubin-induced encephalopathy known as:
questions.rationale: Unconjugated bilirubin crosses the infant blood-brain barrier and causes irreversible Kernicterus.

questions.prompt: In Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) during the initial stabilization phase (F-75), why must high-protein/high-iron feeds be avoided initially?
options: They cause weight gain too slowly
Liver/renal organs cannot handle excess protein/sodium/iron yet (risks heart failure & refeeding shock)
questions.rationale: Start with F-75 cautiously and wait to add Iron until the Rehabilitation (F-100 / RUTF) phase after infections clear.

questions.prompt: What does the Pentavalent vaccine protect Ugandan infants against?
options: Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
Malaria, Typhoid, Cholera, Yellow Fever, Rabies
questions.rationale: DPT-HepB-Hib is given at 6, 10, and 14 weeks of age.

questions.prompt: Which intervention lowers neonatal umbilical cord infection risk in home or rural deliveries?
options: Chlorhexidine 7.1% gel / dry clean cord care
Tightly wrapping the cord in plastic
questions.rationale: Chlorhexidine cord care and clean dry care prevent deadly neonatal tetanus and omphalitis.

questions.prompt: Select ALL components of the IMCI Fever/Malaria Assessment in Uganda:
options: Perform Malaria RDT or blood smear microscopy
Check for stiff neck or bulging fontanelle (meningitis)
Inspect for measles rash, Koplik spots, or ear infection
Give Aspirin to children under 12 with viral fever
questions.rationale: NEVER give Aspirin to children under 16 due to Reye syndrome risk; use Paracetamol.

questions.prompt: Select ALL vaccines administered at 6 weeks of age in Uganda (UNEPI):
questions.rationale: At 6 weeks: OPV1, Pentavalent1, PCV1, and Rota1.

questions.prompt: Select ALL clinical signs of Neonatal Hypoglycemia (< 2.5 mmol/L):
questions.rationale: Both SGA and LGA infants of diabetic mothers are high risk for hypoglycemia.

questions.prompt: Select ALL correct rules for ORS preparation & administration at home:
options: Dissolve 1 standard sachet in 1 liter of clean boiled/cooled water
Discard any unused ORS solution after 24 hours
Give small frequent sips/spoons after every loose stool
Boil the mixed ORS solution again after dissolving
questions.rationale: Never boil ORS after mixing; dissolve in clean cooled water and discard after 24h.

questions.prompt: Phototherapy requires covering the newborn's eyes with opaque eye shields and monitoring hydration status.
questions.rationale: True: eye shields protect the retina and phototherapy increases insensible water loss.

questions.prompt: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) works because sodium and glucose share a co-transporter (SGLT1) across the intestinal mucosa even during secretory diarrhea.
questions.rationale: True: coupled Na+/glucose transport pulls water osmotically into circulation.

questions.prompt: A child with bilateral pitting edema of both feet requires immediate treatment as Moderate Acute Malnutrition (Green MUAC).
questions.rationale: False: nutritional edema is ALWAYS classified as Severe Acute Malnutrition regardless of MUAC.

questions.prompt: Stridor in a resting, calm child is a dangerous sign of upper airway obstruction.
questions.rationale: True: stridor at rest requires urgent airway/steroid/nebulized adrenaline management.

topics.title: Community Health & Microbiology
topics.subtitle: Malaria, HIV, TB, Cholera, Gram stain, sterilization & Uganda HC I–NRH structure

questions.prompt: Which causative protozoan species accounts for the vast majority of severe & fatal Malaria in Uganda?
questions.rationale: P. falciparum transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes causes cerebral and severe malaria.

questions.prompt: At which health facility level in Uganda does the Village Health Team (VHT) operate?
questions.rationale: VHTs form HC I (community level) providing health promotion, ICCM, and referrals.

questions.prompt: What color do Gram-positive bacteria appear under a microscope after standard Gram staining?
questions.rationale: Thick peptidoglycan retains crystal violet-iodine complex, staining purple.

questions.prompt: Which acid-fast stain (Ziehl-Neelsen) is used to identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum?
options: Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) pink/red rods on blue background
questions.rationale: Mycolic acid cell walls retain carbol fuchsin despite acid-alcohol decolorization.

questions.prompt: Classic 'rice-water' painless profuse diarrhea causing rapid fatal hypovolemia is the hallmark of:
questions.rationale: Cholera toxin triggers massive secretory loss; treat immediately with Ringer's Lactate + ORS + Doxycycline/Azithromycin.

questions.prompt: Autoclaving sterilizes surgical instruments by using pressurized saturated steam at:
questions.rationale: Moist heat at 121°C under pressure destroys bacteria, viruses, and heat-resistant endospores.

questions.prompt: Which public health prevention tier focuses on screening tests like Pap smears, HIV testing, and BP checks for early detection?
questions.rationale: Primary = vaccines/clean water; Secondary = early screening; Tertiary = rehabilitation/complication limit.

questions.prompt: Bloody mucoid diarrhea with tenesmus and fever is classically caused by:
questions.rationale: Invasive Shigella damages colonic mucosa causing bloody diarrhea.

questions.prompt: Which opportunistic fungal meningitis is tested via CSF CrAg (Cryptococcal Antigen) and India Ink in advanced HIV (CD4 < 100)?
questions.rationale: CrAg lateral flow assay rapidly detects Cryptococcal meningitis before fatal herniation.

questions.prompt: Which mosquito vector transmits Yellow Fever, Dengue, and Zika viruses (daytime biter)?
questions.rationale: Aedes mosquitoes breed in clean standing containers and transmit arboviruses.

questions.prompt: The 5 Fs of Fecal-Oral disease transmission prevention emphasize breaking spread via:
options: Fingers, Flies, Fields/Soil, Fluids/Water, and Food
questions.rationale: Sanitation (latrines), handwashing, safe water, and fly control halt diarrheal outbreaks.

questions.prompt: A sudden sharp spike of cholera cases above normal endemic baseline within a single district is defined as an:
questions.rationale: Epidemic = cases clearly exceeding expected baseline in a region; Pandemic = multi-continental spread.

questions.prompt: Which vector transmits African Trypanosomiasis (Sleeping Sickness)?
questions.rationale: Tsetse flies transmit Trypanosoma brucei gambiense/rhodesiense.

questions.prompt: What is the cornerstone diagnostic test for Schistosoma mansoni (intestinal bilharzia common around Lake Victoria)?
questions.rationale: S. mansoni ova have a characteristic lateral spine (treat with Praziquantel).

questions.prompt: When handling used syringes/needles on the ward, nurses must:
options: Recap every needle using two hands
Drop uncapped needle immediately into a puncture-proof yellow Sharps Box
questions.rationale: Never recap needles; fill sharps boxes only 3/4 full before sealing.

questions.prompt: Which viral hepatitis forms are primarily spread via contaminated food/water (fecal-oral) rather than blood/sex?
questions.rationale: HAV and HEV spread fecal-orally (HEV carries high mortality in pregnancy).

questions.prompt: In epidemiology, what does 'Incidence Rate' specifically measure?
options: All existing cases (old + new) at a point in time
NEW cases developing in a population at risk during a defined period
questions.rationale: Incidence = new cases over time; Prevalence = total existing old + new cases.

questions.prompt: Under Uganda color-coded medical waste segregation, infectious/anatomical clinical waste goes into which bin?
questions.rationale: Black = general waste; Yellow = infectious waste/sharps box; Red = highly infectious/anatomical.

questions.prompt: Herpes Zoster (shingles) occurs due to reactivation of which latent virus inside dorsal root ganglia?
questions.rationale: VZV reactivates along a unilateral dermatome as painful vesicles (common in immunocompromised patients).

questions.prompt: Select ALL core elements of Primary Health Care (Alma-Ata / Uganda PHC):
options: Treatment of common diseases & essential drugs
questions.rationale: All four are pillars of Uganda's PHC delivery.

questions.prompt: Select ALL preventive measures that interrupt Mother-to-Child Transmission (MTCT) of HIV:
options: Exclusive breastfeeding with maternal viral suppression (or safe replacement)
questions.rationale: Combined maternal ART + infant prophylaxis lowers MTCT below 2%.

questions.prompt: Select ALL diseases targeted by routine Water, Sanitation & Hygiene (WASH) interventions:
questions.rationale: Sickle cell anemia is genetic autosomal recessive, not waterborne.

questions.prompt: Select ALL correct infection control tiers for isolation:
options: Standard precautions apply to ALL patients regardless of diagnosis
Airborne precautions for TB, Measles, Chickenpox
Droplet precautions (surgical mask) for Meningococcal meningitis & Pertussis
Sterile gloves eliminate the need for handwashing after removal
questions.rationale: Hand hygiene is STILL mandatory immediately after glove removal.

questions.prompt: Endotoxins (lipopolysaccharide) are structural components of Gram-negative bacterial outer membranes.
questions.rationale: True: LPS release during Gram-negative lysis triggers septic shock.

questions.prompt: Standard precautions apply only to patients with a confirmed HIV or Hepatitis B diagnosis.
questions.rationale: False: standard precautions apply universally to ALL patients.

questions.prompt: GeneXpert (Xpert MTB/RIF) rapidly detects both Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA and Rifampicin resistance within ~2 hours.
questions.rationale: True: GeneXpert is first-line rapid molecular TB testing across Uganda.

questions.prompt: Antibiotics are effective first-line cures for uncomplicated viral colds and influenza.
questions.rationale: False: antibiotics target bacteria, not viruses; misuse drives antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

topics.title: Mental Health, Ethics & Leadership
topics.subtitle: MSE ASEPTIC exam, suicide precautions, 4 ethical principles, delegation & PICO research

questions.prompt: A patient states: 'Nobody cares if I live, I gave away my belongings and plan to end my life tonight.' What is the nurse's FIRST action?
options: Reassure them everything will be fine tomorrow
Ensure 1:1 continuous direct observation and remove any dangerous objects immediately
Change the subject to hospital food
questions.rationale: A specific suicide plan + giving away belongings signals acute lethal risk requiring 1:1 observation.

questions.prompt: Which ethical principle gives a mentally competent adult the right to refuse a recommended surgical procedure after informed consent?
questions.rationale: Autonomy protects self-determination and voluntary informed consent/refusal.

questions.prompt: Which symptom is an acute Extrapyramidal Side Effect (EPS) caused by typical antipsychotics like Haloperidol?
options: Acute dystonia (neck/eye muscle spasm — torticollis / oculogyric crisis)
questions.rationale: D2 blockade triggers dystonia, akathisia, and parkinsonism (treat acute dystonia with Benzhexol/Benztropine).

questions.prompt: When delegating tasks to a Nursing Assistant / Enrolled Nurse, the Registered Nurse knows that which task CANNOT be delegated?
options: Obtaining routine vital signs on a stable patient
Assisting with bed bath & oral hygiene
Completing the initial admission nursing assessment and formulating care plan diagnoses
questions.rationale: Initial clinical assessment, care planning, IV push drugs, and teaching remain the RN's responsibility.

questions.prompt: In the Mental Status Examination (MSE), asking 'Can you tell me today's date, where we are, and your full name?' tests:
questions.rationale: Orientation to Time, Place, and Person is part of Cognition.

questions.prompt: Which therapeutic communication response encourages a distressed patient to share feelings openly?
options: 'Why did you let yourself fail your exam?'
'Don't worry, everything happens for a reason.'
'Tell me more about what has been weighing on you today.'
questions.rationale: Open-ended, non-judgmental invitations build trust without false reassurance or 'why' interrogation.

questions.prompt: Which life-threatening emergency involves high fever (> 40°C), 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, tachycardia, and unstable BP after starting Haloperidol?
questions.rationale: NMS requires immediately stopping the antipsychotic, cooling, IV fluids, and Dantrolene/Bromocriptine.

questions.prompt: What does the 'PICO' acronym stand for when formulating an Evidence-Based Nursing research question?
questions.rationale: PICO structures clinical literature searches clearly.

questions.prompt: Which ethical principle means 'First, do no harm' (avoiding preventable medication errors or unsafe delegation)?
questions.rationale: Non-maleficence obligates nurses to prevent harm and safeguard patient safety.

questions.prompt: Which leadership style is MOST effective during a sudden cardiac arrest (Code Blue) emergency on the ward?
options: Autocratic / Directive leadership (clear immediate role commands)
questions.rationale: Emergencies require rapid, clear directive coordination; democratic/transformational styles excel in long-term team building.

questions.prompt: A patient believes 'The radio anchor is secretly broadcasting commands about my life.' What type of symptom is this?
questions.rationale: Delusions are fixed false beliefs (referential: neutral broadcasts seem aimed personally).

questions.prompt: Seeing insects crawling on the ceiling when none are physically present is documented as:
questions.rationale: Hallucinations are false sensory perceptions without external stimuli.

questions.prompt: Which nursing ethical value means telling the patient the honest truth about their diagnosis and prognosis?
questions.rationale: Veracity requires truthfulness in nurse-patient communication.

questions.prompt: Confidential patient HIV status may legally/ethically be disclosed WITHOUT consent only when:
options: Clear statutory duty to protect at-risk sexual partners or mandatory public health reporting laws apply
Posted on social media anonymized poorly
questions.rationale: Confidentiality is strict under UNMC ethics unless legal/partner safety mandates apply.

questions.prompt: In research ethics, approval by an Institutional Review Board / REC and UNCST before enrolling human participants ensures:
options: Protection of human dignity, informed consent, and risk-benefit safety
questions.rationale: Ethical review protects vulnerable study participants from coercion or harm.

questions.prompt: Which anxiety disorder manifests as recurrent intrusive thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive rituals (compulsions) like excessive handwashing?
questions.rationale: OCD combines ego-dystonic intrusive thoughts with anxiety-reducing rituals.

questions.prompt: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is administered BEFORE IV glucose in chronic severe alcohol use disorder to prevent:
questions.rationale: Giving glucose without Thiamine precipitates acute Wernicke's encephalopathy (ataxia, confusion, ophthalmoplegia).

questions.prompt: In quality improvement on a maternity ward, what do the 4 steps of the PDSA cycle represent?
questions.rationale: PDSA tests small ward workflow improvements iteratively.

questions.prompt: Which research design provides the HIGHEST level of single-study evidence for evaluating a new drug vs placebo?
questions.rationale: RCTs minimize bias and confounding through randomization (synthesized further by Systematic Reviews/Meta-analyses).

questions.prompt: Select ALL components of the 5 Rights of Clinical Delegation:
questions.rationale: Safe delegation adheres strictly to all 5 Rights.

questions.prompt: Select ALL therapeutic communication techniques:
options: Giving unsolicited moral advice or arguing delusions
questions.rationale: Avoid lecturing, 'why' questions, false reassurance, or arguing delusions.

questions.prompt: Select ALL hallmark symptoms required for a Major Depressive Episode (>= 2 weeks):
options: Persistent depressed mood or anhedonia (loss of pleasure)
questions.rationale: Elevated grandiosity with decreased need for sleep characterizes Mania, not Depression.

questions.prompt: Select ALL ethical duties of a Registered Nurse/Midwife licensed by UNMC:
options: Practice within scope & keep clinical competencies updated
Document accurately and refuse falsified records
Accept bribes for priority queue placement
questions.rationale: Justice and integrity prohibit discrimination or bribes.

questions.prompt: When a hallucinating patient says 'Don't you hear the voices telling me I'm bad?', the nurse should validate the patient's fear while gently stating they do not hear the voices.
questions.rationale: True: never reinforce the hallucination as real, and never dismiss the patient's distress.

questions.prompt: Informed consent can validly be signed by a sedated, heavily intoxicated patient just before anesthesia.
questions.rationale: False: valid consent requires full decision-making capacity, comprehension, and absence of sedative impairment.

questions.prompt: Lithium toxicity is closely precipitated by dehydration, hyponatremia, and NSAIDs.
questions.rationale: True: low sodium increases proximal tubular Lithium reabsorption.

questions.prompt: Transformational nurse leaders inspire teams around shared patient-safety goals and staff mentorship.
questions.rationale: True: transformational leadership improves retention and clinical care quality.

topics.title: First Aid, Triage & Emergency Care
topics.subtitle: BLS/CPR 30:2, choking Heimlich, airway, shock, snakebite, poisoning & disaster triage

questions.prompt: For an unresponsive adult who is NOT breathing and has NO carotid pulse, what is the standard single-rescuer CPR compression-to-breath ratio?
questions.rationale: Deliver 30 compressions (5–6 cm depth, 100–120/min) followed by 2 rescue breaths.

questions.prompt: Which airway maneuver is mandatory for opening the airway of an unconscious patient with a suspected cervical spine injury?
options: Place two pillows under the head
Force fingers blindly down the throat
questions.rationale: Jaw-thrust opens the airway while maintaining in-line cervical immobilization.

questions.prompt: A conscious choking adult cannot speak, cough, or breathe (universal clutching throat sign). Immediate action:
options: Perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) until object clears or unresponsive
questions.rationale: Perform abdominal thrusts (chest thrusts in pregnancy/obesity); start CPR if unresponsive.

questions.prompt: In Disaster Mass-Casualty Triage (START), which tag color goes to a victim with open femoral arterial bleeding & shock who is still breathing?
questions.rationale: Red Immediate receives priority stabilization to survive.

questions.prompt: When a victim suffers an acute venomous Snakebite in rural Uganda, what is the correct pre-hospital First Aid?
options: Cut the bite open and suck out the venom by mouth
Apply a tight rope tourniquet until foot turns cold
Keep patient calm & still, immobilize the bitten limb below heart level, remove rings, and transport rapidly for antivenom
questions.rationale: NEVER cut, suck, or apply tight tourniquets (causes tissue necrosis); immobilize limb and reach hospital.

questions.prompt: For an accidental acid/alkali chemical splash into the eye, what is the immediate priority action?
options: Irrigate continuously with copious clean water or normal saline for at least 15–30 minutes
Attempt to neutralize acid with alkaline drops
questions.rationale: Immediate, prolonged irrigation dilutes and flushes corrosive chemicals.

questions.prompt: Which mnemonic guides the immediate emergency primary survey in trauma and critical care?
questions.rationale: ABCDE treats the greatest threat to life first before moving down the sequence.

questions.prompt: For an adult unconscious patient breathing normally with no suspected spinal trauma, place them in the:
questions.rationale: Recovery position prevents tongue obstruction and aspiration of vomit/saliva.

questions.prompt: Which poisoning toxidrome causes pinpoint pupils (miosis), profuse salivation/sweating, bronchospasm, and bradycardia (DUMBBELSS)?
options: Organophosphate pesticide poisoning (treat with Atropine + Pralidoxime)
questions.rationale: Organophosphate cholinergic crisis requires high-dose IV Atropine until bronchial secretions dry.

questions.prompt: To control severe external arterial hemorrhage from a forearm laceration first, the nurse applies:
options: Direct firm sterile pressure over the wound
questions.rationale: Direct firm pressure arrests > 90% of external bleeding immediately.

questions.prompt: When an AED (Automated External Defibrillator) advises 'Shock Advised', what must the team leader ensure BEFORE pressing Shock?
options: Keep one hand on the patient's chest
Ensure everyone is 'Clear' of touching the patient or metal bed
Turn off oxygen only after shock
questions.rationale: Ensure nobody contacts the patient/conductive surfaces to prevent rescuer electrocution.

questions.prompt: Which sign confirms Tension Pneumothorax (immediate needle decompression emergency)?
options: Absent unilateral breath sounds, severe hypotension, JVD, and tracheal deviation to opposite side
questions.rationale: Needle decompression (2nd ICS midclavicular or 4th/5th anterior axillary) relieves lethal mediastinal shift.

questions.prompt: During an active generalized tonic-clonic seizure, the nurse's SAFE priority is to:
options: Force a wooden tongue blade between clenched teeth
Protect the head, turn patient on side if possible, loosen tight neck clothing, and time the seizure
questions.rationale: NEVER insert objects into the mouth or restrain convulsions; keep airway safe and give IV/rectal Diazepam if > 5 min.

questions.prompt: What blood glucose level in an acutely confused patient confirms Emergency Hypoglycemia needing immediate IV Dextrose?
questions.rationale: Give 25–50 mL IV 50% Dextrose (or 10% Dextrose in children) immediately for unconscious hypoglycemia.

questions.prompt: What is the correct landmark for adult CPR chest compressions?
options: Lower half of the sternum (center of chest between nipples)
questions.rationale: Center of the chest on the lower half of the sternum maximizes cardiac output without xiphoid/liver injury.

questions.prompt: How should an amputated finger/digit be preserved while transporting the patient to surgical theater?
options: Wrap in sterile saline-moistened gauze inside a sealed waterproof bag, placed ON ice
questions.rationale: Never freeze tissue directly on ice; keep cool and moist in a sealed barrier.

questions.prompt: In thermal flame burns on clothing, the first immediate rescue rule is:
options: Stop, Drop, and Roll + cool burn gently with clean cool (not iced) water for 20 minutes
Peel off melted synthetic clothing forcibly
questions.rationale: Cool clean running water halts thermal progression; NEVER apply toothpaste, butter, or cow dung.

questions.prompt: An unconscious patient has a sudden fall in BP to 70/40 and facial swelling minutes after receiving IV Penicillin. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Give Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM STAT, elevate legs, stop the Penicillin infusion immediately, give O2 and fluids.

questions.prompt: Which assessment scale classifies coma depth rapidly in emergencies before calculating full GCS?
questions.rationale: AVPU takes seconds during primary survey D (Disability) check.

questions.prompt: Select ALL essential characteristics of High-Quality Adult CPR:
options: Allow full chest recoil after every compression
Minimize pauses (< 10 seconds) in chest compressions
questions.rationale: High-quality compressions + minimal interruptions double survival odds.

questions.prompt: Select ALL items checked under 'D — Disability' in an Emergency Primary Survey:
options: Pupil size and reactivity to light (PERRLA)
questions.rationale: Always check blood sugar during Disability ('Don't ever forget glucose').

questions.prompt: Select ALL signs of Smoke Inhalation Airway Burn emergency (need early intubation):
options: Singed nasal hairs and facial soot
questions.rationale: Airway edema progresses rapidly after thermal smoke inhalation; prepare early intubation.

questions.prompt: Select ALL immediate management actions for Hypovolemic Hemorrhagic Shock:
options: Control active bleeding via direct pressure
Infuse warm isotonic crystalloids (Ringer's Lactate / 0.9% NaCl)
questions.rationale: Keep patient supine (legs slightly elevated if no head injury) to perfuse the brain.

questions.prompt: For a pregnant woman in obvious third trimester needing CPR, manually displace the uterus to the LEFT to relieve aortocaval compression.
questions.rationale: True: left uterine displacement improves venous return during resuscitation.

questions.prompt: You should routinely perform a blind finger sweep inside an unconscious choking victim's mouth even if you cannot see an object.
questions.rationale: False: blind finger sweeps push foreign bodies deeper into the airway.

questions.prompt: Always cool acute burns with clean cool running water rather than ice water to prevent secondary hypothermia and vasoconstriction.
questions.rationale: True: cool water (15–20°C) for 20 minutes saves tissue without frostbite injury.

questions.prompt: In severe organophosphate poisoning, Atropine is withheld until the heart rate drops below 40 bpm.
questions.rationale: False: start IV Atropine immediately and titrate until lungs clear of secretions and wheezes.

topics.title: Reproductive Health, Gynaecology & Midwifery II
topics.subtitle: Ectopic pregnancy, STI syndromic care, family planning, breech & obstetric emergencies

questions.prompt: A sexually active woman presents with missed period, unilateral lower abdominal pain, positive urine hCG, and dizziness/hypotension. Suspect:
questions.rationale: Amenorrhea + unilateral pain + positive hCG + shock = ruptured ectopic until proven otherwise.

questions.prompt: Which Ugandan STI syndromic management regimen covers BOTH Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis in urethral/cervical discharge?
options: Single-dose Cefixime/Ceftriaxone + Azithromycin or Doxycycline (+ Metronidazole if vaginal)
questions.rationale: Cover gonorrhea + chlamydia simultaneously and treat sexual partners.

questions.prompt: Which contraception method ALSO protects against HIV and sexually transmitted infections (dual protection)?
questions.rationale: Only barrier condoms prevent both pregnancy and STIs/HIV.

questions.prompt: What is the visual cervical screening method widely performed by Ugandan nurses/midwives using 3–5% acetic acid?
questions.rationale: VIA highlights acetowhite cervical lesions rapidly ('See-and-Treat' with cryotherapy/thermal ablation).

questions.prompt: Which maneuver delivers the after-coming head safely in a vaginal breech delivery?
options: Lovset's maneuver for arms, then Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit maneuver for the head
questions.rationale: Lovset rotates shoulders; Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit maintains flexion of the after-coming head.

questions.prompt: When umbilical cord prolapse occurs during labour with a live fetus, what is the immediate midwife emergency action?
options: Push the cord vigorously back into the uterus
Keep gloved hand in vagina lifting presenting part off the cord + place mother in Knee-Chest / steep Trendelenburg until emergency C-section
questions.rationale: Relieve cord compression continuously until emergency cesarean delivery; cover exposed cord with warm sterile saline gauze.

questions.prompt: Which hormone causes the mid-cycle surge (~Day 14 of 28-day cycle) that triggers ovulation?
questions.rationale: A sharp pituitary LH surge triggers follicular rupture and ovulation.

questions.prompt: Uterine Rupture in obstructed labour classically presents with:
options: Sudden tearing abdominal pain, cessation of contractions, fetal distress/absent FHR, easily palpable fetal parts & shock
questions.rationale: Uterine rupture requires immediate laparotomy + resuscitation.

questions.prompt: How long does the Copper T 380A Intrauterine Device (IUD) provide effective reversible contraception?
questions.rationale: The Copper IUD provides highly effective non-hormonal contraception for 10–12 years (and works as emergency contraception within 5 days).

questions.prompt: Emergency Contraceptive Pills (Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg) are most effective when taken within how many hours after unprotected intercourse?
options: Within 72 hours (up to 120 hours for Ulipristal/Copper IUD)
questions.rationale: Sooner within 72 hours gives highest efficacy before ovulation.

questions.prompt: Incomplete miscarriage with fever, foul-smelling products of conception, and lower abdominal tenderness defines:
options: Septic abortion (requires broad-spectrum IV antibiotics + gentle MVA)
questions.rationale: Stabilize with IV antibiotics immediately before manual vacuum aspiration (MVA).

questions.prompt: Classic 'snowstorm' ultrasound appearance with disproportionately large uterus-for-dates, severe vomiting, and very high hCG indicates:
questions.rationale: Evacuate via suction/MVA and monitor serial beta-hCG for 6–12 months.

questions.prompt: Which medication is contraindicated in breastfeeding mothers during the first 6 weeks postpartum because it reduces breastmilk supply?
questions.rationale: Estrogen suppresses milk production and increases postpartum VTE risk early postpartum.

questions.prompt: What is the cardinal sign of Chorioamnionitis during labour?
options: Maternal fever > 38°C, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia (> 160 bpm), and foul amniotic fluid
questions.rationale: Treat promptly with broad-spectrum IV antibiotics and expedite delivery.

questions.prompt: Uterine inversion immediately after 3rd stage delivery requires:
options: Wait for spontaneous correction after 2 hours
Manual uterine replacement under analgesia/tocolysis BEFORE placental removal if still attached + resuscitation
questions.rationale: Replace uterus immediately while calling for emergency obstetric support.
